b: U2 saved the best for last: The band’s 16th studio album, Carnaval de Luz, closes with the meditative “Torn,” a duet between Bono and Dolly Parton. The country legend laid down her part in Nashville in June, less than three months before she died on August 25 at the age of 80.

“We’d no idea it would be her last, but I wonder if she knew,” Bono said of the session on RTÉ, where the track got its first spin on Thursday morning. Two alternate takes, one produced by Parton’s longtime collaborator Kent Wells and another by T Bone Burnett, are out today as well, with the Wells version having premiered on U.S. country radio on Thursday.

Produced by Jacknife Lee, Carnaval de Luz is U2’s first full-length set of new material since 2017’s Songs of Experience and follows this year’s EPs Days of Ash and Easter Lily. In addition to Parton, Rosalía turns up on the track “The Mirror Maker.” The album’s release also marks the 50th anniversary of drummer Larry Mullen Jr. pinning a call for bandmates to a noticeboard at Dublin’s Mount Temple Comprehensive School.
